title: Rectangles, triangles and Schrödinger waves
summary: Can a finite set of lattice points determine many rectangles and few isosceles triangles? This turns out to be a surprisingly interesting question in combinatorial geometry that we answer using basic analytic number theory combined with a finite-field construction. The result is useful because it gives obstructions to Mizohata--Takeuchi-type estimates in the setting of the paraboloid.
